_comment: Registration for scripts/pytest-parallel-differential.py (issue #1086).
WHY THIS GATE NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): its verdict is the acceptance
evidence for running the test suite in parallel, and nothing downstream
re-derives it. Once `-n 8` is in `make test` and in CI, every later green is
read as 'the same tests passed' on the strength of one comparison made once.
An agreeing verdict from an instrument that has never been shown to DISAGREE is
not evidence - it is the same bytes a broken comparator prints.
THE CASES ARE PAIRS OF JUNIT REPORTS, which is what the gate consumes, so a
case directory holds `serial.xml` and `parallel.xml` and the invocation is
`--pair {case}`. They are hand-written and tiny: the question is whether the
gate can tell an agreeing pair from a disagreeing one, not whether it can
handle 4,263 nodes.
BOTH BAD CASES CARRY AN IDENTICAL TALLY ON PURPOSE, and that is the whole
design rather than a convenience. The anchor below compares how many passed
and how many failed - the reading issue #1086 names and rejects in one
sentence, 'the same pass/fail SET, not merely the same colour'. A bad case
whose totals differ would be caught by that anchor, the control would report
INERT, and the demonstration would establish nothing about the distinction
this gate exists to draw.
bad-substituted-node  3 passes on both sides, and a different test ran. The
MEMBERSHIP FLOOR direction: a worker that collects a
different population prints the same colour and the
same count, and only the node-id SET separates them.
bad-dangerous-flip    1 pass and 1 failure on both sides, swapped between
two tests - so one FAILS serially and PASSES in
parallel. That is the direction that must block:
whatever made it pass was not the code under test.
THE GOOD CASE CARRIES A FAILURE PRESENT IN BOTH RUNS, deliberately. The real
measurement for #1086 had exactly one - an environmental failure reproducing
identically serially and in parallel - and a good case of all-green would
leave the gate's ability to accept an AGREEING failure unexercised. THE HALF
THAT MATTERS for a gate wedged at 'disagree': a comparator that rejects every
pair passes both bad cases on its own, and this gate's red is what would stop
a parallelism change from shipping.
Stdlib-only, offline and git-free, like the gate: the slim CI image gives the
same verdict as a dev box, so `negative-controls` is not a weaker run of this
control than `make verify` is.

cases.name: bad-substituted-node
cases.why: Both reports carry three passing tests and zero failures, and `tests.test_beta::test_three` was replaced by `tests.test_beta::test_four`. Every count agrees; the population does not. If this scores GOOD the membership floor is not being checked at all, and a worker that silently collects a different set of tests is indistinguishable here from one that collects the right set.

cases.name: bad-dangerous-flip
cases.why: Identical node-id sets, identical tallies (1 pass, 1 failure both times), and the pass and the failure belong to DIFFERENT tests in the two runs - so `test_two` fails serially and passes in parallel. That is the dangerous direction: a real red converted into a silent green for as long as the parallelism holds. If this scores GOOD the gate is comparing colour rather than verdicts.

cases.name: good-matched
cases.why: Identical node-id sets and identical per-node verdicts, INCLUDING one test that fails in both runs - the shape the real #1086 measurement had. THE HALF THAT MATTERS for a comparator wedged at 'disagree': one that rejected every pair would satisfy both bad cases on its own and would block every future parallelism change with a red that means nothing. It also exercises the accept-an-agreeing-failure path, which an all-green good case would leave unproven.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the gate is new and never shipped blind, so there is no revision to vendor - `--verify-provenance` therefore reports `unverified`, which is correct and must never be read as `ok`. This is the FIRST FRAMING on the record: 'did the two runs agree' answered by comparing how many passed and how many failed, which is both the obvious thing to write and exactly what a human does glancing at two summary lines. It misses `bad-substituted-node` because the counts match while the population differs, misses `bad-dangerous-flip` because the counts match while the verdicts moved between tests, and agrees with the real gate on `good-matched`, which is what makes the demonstration isolated rather than merely different.
